analysis:
Both changed files are CI test scripts under .github/scripts: test-threat-bedrock.py (new workload call-policy and large-scan tests, plus Scanner and ThreatContext imports) and test-threat-budget.py (manual-rerun handoff, runtime bound and workload-ceiling tests). They add no production provider, coordinator, or native-runtime code, so none of the provider-side assets or boundaries (TB-002, TB-011, A-001..A-017) are directly altered.

The tests assert fail-closed behavior in the review tooling. Workload call policy rejects unplanned native calls (lines 301-316). Invalid policies and a ceiling above 100 raise ReviewUnavailable (333-340). The emergency ceiling stops before the unadmitted stage (318-331). A manual rerun (GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2) does no paid work and yields a report that clean() rejects (budget test patch). THREAT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is bounded to 60-3000. Merge-policy tests still require that incomplete scans, stale runs, non-members, and bot or self reviews never clear; MemberGateTests use a separate membership token.

The tests use synthetic data and fake clients. They do not weaken any assertion that I can see, and the ledger privacy checks (no source or reasoning in the usage file) are retained.

I cannot see the production implementations (threat_review/bedrock.py, budget_scan.py, threat-model-review.py runtime_seconds, and the new workload policy and MANUAL_SCAN_RERUN_DISABLED paths). Whether those match the tests is outside the supplied evidence. One thing to verify: the 100-call workload ceiling and the 50-minute runtime limit are enforced in the real code, not only in the tests. No concrete security regression is identified.
